description: A small plugin library with a command line, published on PyPI by three maintainers at version 1.5.0, with a changelog, a CI workflow, and tests. Four gaps are seeded, each at one place: a migration from config_loader to settings.read that nothing ends or checks, a rollout flag that outlived its rollout, a minor release that removed a command-line option without a deprecation, and an issue workflow that writes the issue title into a shell command. With three maintainers, neither the flag nor the migration names an owner.

must_find.QUAL-11: docs/decisions.md retires config_loader with no completion condition and no check against new uses, and hooks.py, the newest module, still calls config_loader.load()
must_find.STRUCT-04: the lazy_load rollout ended in 1.3.0, yet the setting still reaches the eager path in loader.py, which no test runs
must_find.DEL-03: 1.4.0, a minor release of a package past 1.0, removed the --format option of list with no earlier deprecation
must_find.CI-10: the issues-opened workflow writes github.event.issue.title into a shell command through an expression, so an outsider's title runs with the job's token
must_find.TEAM-03: three people maintain the project, and neither the lazy_load setting nor the config_loader migration names an owner

must_not_flag.SEC-05: no credentials anywhere; the workflow's token is the one GitHub provides
must_not_flag.STRUCT-02: fewer than 20 files in every directory
must_not_flag.TOOL-01: no tools, skills, or MCP servers configured
must_not_flag.OPS-01: a library, not a deployed service

defects.description: hooks.py, added in 1.5.0 after decision 3 retired config_loader, still calls config_loader.load(), and nothing ends the migration or rejects new uses
The lazy_load rollout ended in 1.3.0, but the setting still reaches the eager path, and no test runs it
1.4.0, a minor release, removed the --format option of list with no earlier deprecation
The issues-opened workflow writes the issue title into a shell command through a ${{ }} expression
